meetings.title: Part 4 Durham County Budget Proposal FY12-13
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 4 of the FY 2012-13 County Manager's Recommended Budget presentation, the County Manager detailed recommended funding increases for Durham Public Schools ($115.8 million current expense, $1.37 million capital outlay, and $28.9 million in school debt service) alongside initiatives aligned with Strategic Plan Goals 2 through 5. Key recommendations included adding three public health nurses for elementary school well-child screenings in partnership with Duke Health System, replacing 35 Sheriff's Office vehicles, studying county fire tax district consolidation, expanding environmental staffing and open space funding to $500,000, and reorganizing county customer service and lobby staffing. The County Manager concluded by challenging the Board of Commissioners to place a study of Durham City-County government consolidation on a future work session agenda and announcing the June 2012 public hearing, work sessions, and June 25 budget adoption schedule.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools FY 2012-13 Operating, Capital, and Debt Service Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager reported that improved quarter-cent sales tax projections enabled him to recommend $244,880 more in current expense funding for Durham Public Schools than the district had requested. Proposed FY 2012-13 appropriations total $115.8 million for current expense and $1,370,000 for capital outlay, plus $28.9 million in school-related debt service (a $2.9 million increase following spring bond sales). Per-pupil funding is projected to rise by $120 over the current year to $3,165 per pupil, keeping Durham County's per-pupil contribution higher than any other urban county in North Carolina.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Goal 2 (Healthy Durham): Community Health Assessment and Duke Health Partnership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Public Health department representative presented findings from the Durham County Community Health Assessment, noting lower adult smoking and secondhand smoke exposure and improved youth dental access, while highlighting disparities in cancer, heart disease, HIV rates, obesity, and the 33% uninsured rate. Upcoming initiatives include community gardens and mobile farmers markets to address food deserts, prescription drug drop boxes, an August 1 county smoke-free ordinance, targeted mental health outreach for Hispanic and LGBTQ youth, and expanded adult dental care through Project Access ($320,000 annual county support). The County Manager also recommended partnering with Duke Health System ($60,000 donation) and using home health license sale reserves to fund three public health nurses for well-child screenings in three elementary schools.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Goal 3 (Safety): Sheriff's Office Outreach, Vehicle Replacements, and Fire District Consolidation Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Mike Andrews reported a decline in county crime rates and highlighted community engagement tools including the Sheriff's Office Facebook page launched in March, expanded Community Watch coordination with Durham Police PAC units, task force assignments with DPD and the FBI, and the public RAIDS Online crime mapping portal. The County Manager noted the Sheriff's fleet had not been replaced in three years and budgeted funds to replace 35 aging vehicles. He also announced an agreement with fire chiefs across the county's five fire tax districts to study consolidating fire services to improve efficiency and potentially lower residents' fire insurance premiums.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Goal 4 (Environment): Sustainability Staffing, Jordan/Falls Lake Rules, and Open Space Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Building on the joint City-County greenhouse gas reduction plan, the County Manager and City Manager Tom Bonfield recommended adding a new sustainability position focused on engaging private-sector businesses to lower carbon emissions. The budget also adds two positions—one in Public Health and one in the County Engineer's office—to meet state-mandated Jordan Lake and Falls Lake water quality rules. Additionally, the Manager proposed increasing annual pay-as-you-go funding for open space and farmland protection from $300,000 to $500,000 (after reducing it from $850,000 in FY 2011) without issuing debt.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Goal 5 (Accountable Government): Customer Service Consolidation, Security-to-Greeter Transition, Branding, and HR Staffing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To improve efficiency and customer service, the County Manager proposed cutting directory listings from scores of phone numbers to eight core numbers—saving part of an existing $60,000 expense—and adding a call taker to the Tax Administration call center (919-560-0300) to route calls alongside workforce-wide customer service training. He also recommended eliminating one security officer in the Administration building on September 30 and reducing Human Services building security from 7.5 to 4.25 officers on January 1 to fund five lobby customer service greeters (three at Human Services and two at Administration). Finally, he previewed the county's new branding and upcoming website redesign, and requested an organizational development position in Human Resources to drive cultural change.

agenda_items.title: Proposal to Study Durham City-County Government Consolidation and FY 2012-13 Budget Adoption Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In his closing remarks, the County Manager urged the Board of Commissioners to reconsider unifying Durham City and County governments into a single government, arguing that significant long-term savings and efficiencies beyond incremental collaboration require consolidation and asking commissioners to place the topic on a future work session agenda. He announced that proposed budget copies would be available at the Clerk's office, County Manager's office, county libraries, and online the next morning. He outlined the upcoming schedule: work sessions on May 31, June 4, June 12, and (if needed) June 14; a public hearing on June 11 at 7:00 p.m.; and final budget adoption on June 25.

meetings.title: Part 3 Durham County Budget Proposal FY12-13
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 3 of the FY 2012-13 County Manager's Recommended Budget presentation, the County Manager emphasized citizen collaboration and alignment between the budget and the newly adopted Strategic Plan, including $92,295 for first-year strategic planning initiatives. Under Strategic Plan Goal 1 (Prosperity), economic development staff reported over 2,300 announced jobs and $475 million in new investment in the prior year alongside major 2012 expansions by AW North Carolina, Cree, and BASF. The Manager proposed 48.5 new county positions requiring only $299,382 in new local county funds, and featured education leaders explaining how quarter-cent sales tax proceeds support Durham Public Schools classrooms, pre-K education, and Durham Technical Community College student stipends and workforce training grants.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Collaboration and Strategic Plan Implementation Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the Begin Again testimonial, the County Manager reflected on Durham's tradition of vocal citizen participation and interactive governance. He introduced a video segment featuring Dr. Tyrone Baines explaining the recently adopted Strategic Plan, which was shaped by approximately 3,000 residents and county employees. The Manager noted that the FY 2012-13 budget includes $92,295 for first-year strategic planning initiatives and structures the budget presentation around the plan's five goal areas.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Goal 1 (Prosperity): Economic Development and Job Growth Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Addressing job creation priorities under Goal 1, economic development coordinator Marquita Welton reported that Durham County's collaborative partnerships with businesses, universities, nonprofits, and the City yielded more than 2,300 announced jobs and over $475 million in new investment last year, including 175 jobs and $70 million from United Therapeutics in Research Triangle Park. She noted strong early 2012 announcements from AW North Carolina (250 jobs), Cree, and BASF, while highlighting Durham's low unemployment rate and key attractors such as Durham Tech, Duke University, North Carolina Central University's biotechnology program, DPAC, and the Durham Bulls Athletic Park.

agenda_items.title: Proposed 48.5 New County Positions and Funding Breakdown
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager proposed adding 48.5 new county government positions in FY 2012-13, including paramedics, nurses, environmental specialists, maintenance personnel, and staff assistants. He explained that only $299,382 in new local county tax dollars would be needed to fund these roles, with the remainder covered by grants, the termination of EMS contracts with two county fire departments, increased EMS call volume revenues, and operational efficiency savings.

agenda_items.title: Quarter-Cent Sales Tax Funding for Durham Public Schools, Pre-K, and Durham Tech
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Connecting education to economic prosperity, the County Manager highlighted quarter-cent sales tax funding for Durham Public Schools, Durham Technical Community College, and pre-K education as a critical dropout-prevention investment. In video remarks, DPS representative Dr. Eric B. Coates explained that sales tax proceeds go directly to classrooms for teachers, counselors, and school-based support staff to maintain operations and prevent larger class sizes. Durham Tech representative Dr. Bill Ingram detailed plans to use sales tax dollars for campus service stipends providing financial aid and work experience to low-income Durham County graduates, alongside direct grants for adults returning for job training or retraining.

meetings.title: Part 1 Durham County Budget Proposal FY12-13
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 1 of the FY 2012-13 County Manager's Recommended Budget presentation, the County Manager opened before Chair Michael D. Page and the Board of Commissioners by presenting a $347.4 million General Fund budget with no property tax rate increase, holding the rate at 74.59 cents. Although total General Fund spending reflects a nominal 3.10% reduction due to shifting over $25.1 million in mental health services through a merger with Wake County, real spending on county services rises by 4.22%. The Manager also highlighted national rankings honoring Durham's economy, diversity, arts, and food scene, and concluded the segment with a video showcasing a county employee wellness flash mob at CCB Plaza.

agenda_items.title: FY 2012-13 Recommended General Fund Budget and Tax Rate Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Addressing Chair Michael D. Page, the County Manager presented the recommended FY 2012-13 General Fund budget of $347.4 million and proposed keeping the county property tax rate unchanged at 74.59 cents per $100 valuation. He clarified that the apparent 3.10% budget reduction results from merging Durham's mental health services with Wake County, which removed over $25.1 million in expenditures from the county budget. Excluding that transfer, real spending for county services increases by 4.22%.

agenda_items.title: Durham County National Recognitions and Economic Standing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager cited a series of national accolades recognizing Durham as a business-friendly, diverse, and desirable community, including rankings from Forbes, Triangle Business Journal, The Daily Beast, Yahoo Travel, CNN Money, National Jurist, Kiplinger's, Pollstar (recognizing DPAC as fourth most attended in its size range), Southern Living, and the American Farmland Trust. He framed these achievements as evidence of strong local institutions and strategic public investments.

agenda_items.title: County Employee Workforce Culture and Wellness Flash Mob Showcase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Praising county staff as high-performing and dedicated, the County Manager noted that the county promotes a healthy and engaging workplace culture despite demanding workloads. He introduced a video clip of county employees participating in a 15-minute wellness flash mob at CCB Plaza downtown to promote daily physical activity and public awareness of county services.

meetings.title: Part 2 Durham County Budget Proposal FY12-13
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 2 of the FY 2012-13 County Manager's Recommended Budget presentation, the County Manager outlined workforce compensation and wellness investments, including normal performance-based raises, no benefit reductions, a modest 2.4% employee health care cost increase, and restored 37.5-hour weekly employee wellness clinic access with no copays and discounted generics. He highlighted nearly $263 million in county downtown Durham capital investments since 2003—including DPAC, the South Parking Deck, the $90 million Human Services building, and the $119 million new courthouse opening in January 2013—alongside over $36 million in planned courthouse remodeling and Main Library renovations. He also presented the Board's adopted Strategic Vision and recommended adding two new positions to the Begin Again / Project Restore initiative helping formerly incarcerated residents and people in recovery transition into permanent county employment.

agenda_items.title: Employee Compensation, Health Benefits, and Wellness Clinic Restoration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager reported that the FY 2012-13 budget funds normal performance-based raises and preserves county employee benefits with no reductions, incorporating a 2.4% increase in the employee share of health care costs. He announced that employee wellness clinic hours will be restored to 37.5 hours per week with same-day appointments, zero copay, and discounted generic prescriptions filled down the hall at the Public Health pharmacy to lower insurance claims. He also noted that Phase 2 of the Human Services building, opening in early 2013, will include employee shower and exercise facilities.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Capital Investments and New Courthouse Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing Durham County's role in revitalizing downtown Durham, the County Manager noted nearly $263 million in capital investments since 2003, including the 1% occupancy tax that funded over 80% of DPAC's capital cost, the $15 million South Parking Deck for American Tobacco, the $90 million Human Services building housing roughly 800 employees, and the $119 million new courthouse and parking deck opening in January 2013. Sheriff Mike Andrews spoke on the 11-story courthouse design, explaining that consolidating public services on the first three floors and adding 11 recently granted positions will improve security, efficiency, and public navigation.

agenda_items.title: Future Downtown Capital Projects: Courthouse Remodel and Main Library Renovation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager outlined more than $36 million in additional downtown capital investments once the new courthouse opens. The existing courthouse will be completely remodeled into county office space to eliminate leased facilities for county and state services, and renovations to the Main Library—which drew 515,000 visitors compared to DPAC's 414,000 in 2011—will begin in 2015.

agenda_items.title: County Strategic Vision and Expansion of Project Restore / Begin Again Ex-Offender Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reciting the Board's formally adopted Strategic Vision for a thriving, vibrant, and diverse community, the County Manager shared a personal family story about barriers faced by people with felony convictions. He recommended adding two more training positions—doubling the current two slots—in the county's Begin Again / Project Restore initiative, which places ex-offenders and residents recovering from addiction into temporary county jobs with pathways to permanent employment. General Services Solid Waste employee Larry Parker gave a video testimonial recounting how entering Project Restore after federal prison led to a permanent county Maintenance Tech I position.
